title: Carpark-to-nightclub conversion: consent refused on whole-building seismic grounds (Napier)
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE, Building Act 2004): comparative test only; not an Alberta case; no Alberta applicability asserted
code_edition: NZ Building Act s115 change-of-use test; Building Code clauses as cited (B1, H1)
document_type: MBIE determination under Building Act 2004 s188 (regulator decision on an individual matter); not an applicant's alternative-solution file

facts.text: Consent refused for internal alterations converting a carpark area to a nightclub; the authority's reason was that the whole building had to be upgraded for seismic performance under s115 (change of use).
Building is a 1931 wool store: steel column and truss sawtooth roof, reinforced concrete ground beams, partly two storeys with a timber-on-steel intermediate floor.

Detailed seismic assessment (2 February 2019) rated the building 36%NBS, with likely failure at the roof diaphragm transferring loads to the bracing; higher rating would need significant roof-structure work.
Fit-out cost about $60,000; the authority's view was that a proposal not increasing 36%NBS did not comply as nearly as reasonably practicable.
